title: Derived internal-Hom substitution with coefficient and signed-shift comparisons
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], using its constructible exceptional adjunctions and finite-Tor categories $C_\Lambda(T)=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Integral operations are completed; field operations are the specified rationalizations and common finite-stage operations. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].
Use the actual derived internal Homs $H_\Lambda(M,U)=R\mathcal H om_X(M,U)$ and ordinary direct image $Rf_{\Lambda*}$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For $U,V\in C_\Lambda(X)$ and an isomorphism $c:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$, put $J_U(M)=Rf_{\Lambda*}H_\Lambda(M,U)$ and
$$j_c(M)=Rf_{\Lambda*}H_\Lambda(1_M,c):J_U(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_V(M)\qquad(M\in C_\Lambda(X)).$$
These components form a natural isomorphism of contravariant functors. For the signed source-shift comparisons $s_U(M,r):J_U(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}J_U(M)[-r]$ of the actual derived Hom and direct image, for every $r\in\mathbf Z$,
$$s_V(M,r)\circ j_c(M[r])=j_c(M)[-r]\circ s_U(M,r).$$
The source-shift convention on a degree-$d$ Hom family is reindexing with multiplier $(-1)^{rd}$, localized to the derived category; field-stage comparisons are its rationalized or common-stage images.

For an allowed (A5) coefficient comparison $T_X,T_Y$ at $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$, let
$$h_{M,U}:T_XH_\Lambda(M,U)\longrightarrow H_{\Lambda'}(T_XM,T_XU)$$
be the canonical comparison obtained by applying $T_X$ to evaluation, inserting its tensor comparison, and transposing. Let $\gamma_Z:T_YRf_{\Lambda*}Z\to Rf_{\Lambda'*}T_XZ$ be the ordinary direct-image comparison, normalized as the mate of the pullback comparison. For $U',V'\in C_{\Lambda'}(X)$, isomorphisms $u:T_XU\xrightarrow{\sim}U'$, $v:T_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}V'$ and $c':U'\xrightarrow{\sim}V'$ satisfying $v\circ T_Xc=c'\circ u$, set
$$\sigma_{U,u}(M)=Rf_{\Lambda'*}\bigl(H_{\Lambda'}(1,u)\circ h_{M,U}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{H_\Lambda(M,U)}:T_YJ_U(M)\longrightarrow Rf_{\Lambda'*}H_{\Lambda'}(T_XM,U').$$
Define $\sigma_{V,v}$ identically. Then the specified evaluation-defined comparisons satisfy
$$\sigma_{V,v}(M)\circ T_Y(j_c(M))=j_{c'}(T_XM)\circ\sigma_{U,u}(M).$$
These are equations in the actual coefficient category, or its ambient derived realization, with the canonical associators inserted. They use only the domains of (A5); no assertion that arbitrary ambient internal-Hom coefficient comparisons are invertible is included. At integral coefficients the completed comparison is used, and field comparisons are formed by rationalization and common finite stages.

proof.text: Write $H=H_\Lambda$, $R=Rf_{\Lambda*}$ and $R'=Rf_{\Lambda'*}$. Work in the actual ambient derived realizations whenever an output is not in the finite-Tor subcategory. At finite and integral coefficients $H$ is the ringed-site derived Hom, hence a bifunctor; at field coefficients its action on morphisms is the specified rationalized or common-stage action. $R,R'$ are the specified direct-image functors. The only coefficient data used below are the evaluation-transpose definition of $h$, the natural tensor comparison used in that definition, and the direct-image mate $\gamma$ from the question. The allowed domains are those of (A5); this proof does not enlarge them.

proof.text: For $a:M'\to M$, bifunctoriality gives $H(a,1_V)H(1_M,c)=H(1_{M'},c)H(a,1_U)=H(a,c)$. Applying $R$ gives the contravariant naturality square for $j_c$. Likewise $H(1,c^{-1})H(1,c)=1$ and $H(1,c)H(1,c^{-1})=1$, so the components $j_{c^{-1}}$ are the inverse natural transformation. This constructs the asserted natural isomorphism, rather than merely proving its components invertible.

proof.text: Represent $M$ by a complex $L$ and write $I(-)$ for the functorial K-injective replacement of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], so $H(M,U)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I(U))$. The stipulated source-shift comparison is the localization of the chain map $\rho_{L,I}:\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L[r],I)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I)[-r]$ which reindexes a degree-$d$ family $(\phi^p)_p$ and multiplies it by $(-1)^{rd}$. It is a chain isomorphism: the inverse reindexes back with the same sign, and with the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex] and $d_{L[r]}=(-1)^rd_L$ both $\rho(d\phi)$ and $(-1)^rd(\rho\phi)$ equal $(-1)^{r(d+1)}$ times the reindexed $d_I\phi-(-1)^{d+r}\phi d_L$. Its localization is the isomorphism $t_U:H(M[r],U)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(M,U)[-r]$, the inverse of the natural source-shift isomorphism recorded in [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-left] (no boundedness or K-flatness is needed). For a chain map $g:I\to I'$, postcomposition with the degree-zero map $g$ is componentwise [def-pur-hom-complex], and $g((-1)^{rd}\phi)=(-1)^{rd}(g\phi)$, so $\rho_{L,I'}\circ g_*=g_*[-r]\circ\rho_{L,I}$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $H(1,c)$ is the morphism induced through the localization by the functor on pairs of complexes; it is a composite of images of chain maps and of inverses of images of quasi-isomorphisms, and $\rho$ commutes with each, hence with their inverses. Therefore $t_VH(1,c)=H(1,c)[-r]t_U$ for the stipulated signed comparison itself; no chain representative of $c$ and no identification with an unspecified objectwise isomorphism is used. Write $\kappa_Z:R(Z[-r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(RZ)[-r]$ for the canonical direct-image shift comparison occurring in $s$. By definition $s_U=\kappa_{H(M,U)}R(t_U)$. Naturality of this shift comparison says $\kappa_{H(M,V)}R(H(1,c)[-r])=R(H(1,c))[-r]\kappa_{H(M,U)}$. Apply $R$ to the equation for $t$ and substitute this naturality identity; the result is exactly $s_Vj_c(M[r])=j_c(M)[-r]s_U$.

proof.text: Put $T=T_X$ and write $\mu:TH(M,U)\otimes TM\to T(H(M,U)\otimes M)$ for the tensor comparison in the definition of $h$. Use the tensor-Hom transposition supplied for these evaluation maps, with evaluation $e_{M,U}:H(M,U)\otimes M\to U$. The closed adjunction gives $e_{M,V}(H(1,c)\otimes1)=c\,e_{M,U}$. Uncurry the two maps $h_{M,V}\,T H(1,c)$ and $H'(1,Tc)\,h_{M,U}$, both from $TH(M,U)$ to $H'(TM,TV)$. Naturality of $\mu$ makes the first uncurry equal to $T(e_{M,V})\,T(H(1,c)\otimes1)\,\mu=T(c)\,T(e_{M,U})\,\mu$. Naturality of target evaluation and the defining transpose equation for $h_{M,U}$ give exactly this same uncurry for the second map. Injectivity of the tensor-Hom bijection proves $h_{M,V}\,T H(1,c)=H'(1,Tc)\,h_{M,U}$. This is a direct calculation with the evaluation-defined maps, and does not require either $h$ to be an isomorphism.

proof.text: Abbreviate $b_U=H'(1,u)h_{M,U}$ and $b_V=H'(1,v)h_{M,V}$. Postcompose the equation of Step 4 by $H'(1,v)$ and use the given equation $v\,Tc=c'u$. Bifunctoriality gives $b_V\,T H(1,c)=H'(1,v\,Tc)h_{M,U}=H'(1,c'u)h_{M,U}=H'(1,c')b_U$. This also verifies every source and target: both sides go from $TH(M,U)$ to $H'(TM,V')$.

proof.text:
The mate definition makes $\gamma:T_YR\to R'T_X$ a natural transformation. Apply its naturality to $a=H(1,c)$ to obtain $\gamma_{H(M,V)}\,T_YR(a)=R'T_X(a)\,\gamma_{H(M,U)}$. Using Step 5, functoriality of $R'$ and associativity now gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_{V,v}\,T_Y(j_c)&=R'(b_V)\,\gamma_{H(M,V)}\,T_YR(a)\\
&=R'(b_V\,T_Xa)\,\gamma_{H(M,U)}\\
&=R'(H'(1,c')\,b_U)\,\gamma_{H(M,U)}\\
&=j_{c'}(T_XM)\,\sigma_{U,u}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $j_{c'}(T_XM)=R'H'(1,c')$ is precisely the target-stage substitution in the statement. The computation uses the specified mate itself, with no choice of a different direct-image comparison.

source.place: Step 3, naturality of the specified mate and substitution; formal pasting of the two displayed naturality equations.

proof.text: At integral coefficients the argument takes place in the completed coefficient category or its actual ambient derived realization: $h$ is its stipulated evaluation transpose and $\gamma$ its stipulated completed mate. Steps 4--6 compare morphisms in that category directly; they never infer equality from equality of finite reductions. For $E$, use the rationalized actions on objects and morphisms specified for $H$ and $R$: composition and identities in each displayed calculation are preserved, and the degree-zero evaluation and shift comparisons are their specified images. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent the finitely many objects and arrows in a displayed calculation over a single finite extension containing their stages. The common-stage formula for operations conjugates each arrow by its endpoint comparison. In a composite the adjacent comparison and its inverse cancel, so each equation proved over that stage gives the displayed equation of common-stage classes. The allowed coefficient comparison from (A5) is used only where $h$ and $\gamma$ are defined. In particular no reduction from a field to finite coefficients, no perfectness of $M$ on the site, and no invertibility of an arbitrary internal-Hom comparison is used.
